{{2019–20 Mid-American Conference men's basketball standings}}

The '''2019–20 Ohio University Bobcats men's basketball team''' represented [[Ohio University]] for the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bobcats were led by first-year head coach [[Jeff Boals]], who was a 1995 graduate of Ohio University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|title=Men's Basketball|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16|archive-date=2019-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191016173856/https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/coaches/index|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/coaches/jeff-boals-1.html|title=Jeff Boals|website=Sports Reference|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/20190318ld8207 |title=Ohio Athletics Officially Introduces Boals As Men's Basketball Head Coach - Ohio University |website=www.ohiobobcats.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328110718/http://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/releases/20190318ld8207 |archive-date=2019-03-28}}</ref> The team played their home games at the [[Convocation Center (Ohio University)|Convocation Center]] in [[Athens, Ohio]] as a member of the East Division of the [[Mid-American Conference]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ohio.edu/building-directory/convocation-center|title=Convocation Center|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2022-09-29}}</ref> They finished the season 17–15, 8–10 in MAC play to finish in last place in the East division. As the No. 8 seed in the [[2020 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they defeated [[2019–20 Central Michigan Chippewas men's basketball team|Central Michigan]] in the first round before the tournament was canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2019-20 Ohio Men's Basketball Schedule|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/schedule|access-date=2020-10-16|website=Ohio University|language=en|archive-date=2020-01-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111203927/https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2019-20/schedule|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Previous season==

{{main|2018–19 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team}}

The [[2018–19 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team|Bobcats]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 14–17, 6–12 in [[2018–19 Mid-American Conference men's basketball season|MAC play]] to finish in last place in the East Division. As the No. 10 seed in the [[2019 MAC men's basketball tournament|MAC tournament]], they were defeated in the first round by [[2018–19 Northern Illinois Huskies men's basketball team|Northern Illinois]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohiobobcats.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/schedule|title=2018-19 Ohio Men's Basketball Schedule|website=Ohio University|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16}}</ref>

On March 13, 2019, head coach [[Saul Phillips (basketball)|Saul Phillips]] was fired. He finished his five-year tenure at Ohio with an 81–77 overall record.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.athensnews.com/news/sports/ou-cans-its-highest-paid-employee/article_6f955f48-45b9-11e9-99cb-dbe75af5b97c.html|title=OU cans its highest-paid employee|last=Harrison|first=Alexander|website=The Athens NEWS|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16}}</ref> Five days later, the school named Ohio alum Jeff Boals, head coach at [[2018–19 Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball team|Stony Brook]], as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cantonrep.com/sports/20190318/jeff-boals-lands-dream-job-at-ohio-university|title=Jeff Boals lands 'dream job' at Ohio University|last=Popovich|first=Mike|website=The Repository|language=en|access-date=2019-10-16}}</ref>
